The papersThe code

Pathway prognosis, dug back up.

We rebuilt the lost pipeline from the paper and reran it on the four public data sets. Of 57 results, 53 were attempted: 0 came back exact, 14 agree, 21 partly, 7 inconclusive and 11 differ.

Our LASSO keeps 5 pathways, 3 of them the paper's (SRCRPTP, RARRXR, IL5); the paper keeps 15. The selection follows from the scores, and our scores of the paper's pathways are not the paper's (table2.genomic_univariate). The paper's coefficients applied to our scores give Miller p 2.3e-4 and AUC 0.66 (printed 6.25e-12 and 0.80). Our pathway scores are not the paper's: of the 15 pathways of Table 2, 4 have a univariate Cox p within one order of magnitude of the printed one on our scores, and VIP, LYSOSOME, AKAP13 and LINOLEIC ACID, printed p 2e-6 to 4e-3, have p 0.5 to 0.8. pathifier is deterministic here (seeds 1 to 3 give the same scores), and no preprocessing variant we tried brings these pathways back. The paper's pathifier run, gene mapping and MSigDB release are not available. The same four features are selected; the coefficients differ by 0.0003 to 0.049. The penalty is the median of 250 random cross-validations (ours 7.32); its exact value depends on the folds, which the paper does not give. Lymph node and size are kept and grade and p53 are not, as in the paper; 4 of our 5 genomic pathways are kept (paper: 10 of 15). The pathway count follows from our genomic model (table2.genomic).

The models are fitted on our pathway scores, which are not the paper's (table2.genomic_univariate): our genomic model keeps 5 pathways, not 15. It reaches Miller p 1.1e-7 and AUC 0.73 (printed 6.25e-12, 0.80), Pawitan 5.4e-4 (3.91e-5), Ivshina 1.9e-6 (1.52e-4) and Desmedt 0.69 (3.73e-4); Ivshina's AUC is the paper's. Ivshina is not an independent test set: 232 of its 249 arrays are Miller's (GSE4922 re-deposits GSE3494's arrays), which may be why it is the only test set where we do better than printed. The curves follow our model, not the paper's; see fig4.values.

Text: pathway-based models beat gene-based models on all four sets
pathway-based better than gene-based (lower p and higher AUC) in 1 of 4 sets: pawitan, Differs

The pathway models are fitted on our pathway scores, which are not the paper's (table2.genomic_univariate); the gene models on our gene-level expression, whose mapping and normalization may differ from the paper's (biomaRt through RefSeq, CONOR), so Pawitan's and Ivshina's gene models differ too. Desmedt has almost no relapse signal in our hands: no pathway has univariate p below 0.008 and no gene below 3.4e-5 (of 7,455 expressed), so cross-validation picks a penalty (pathways 4.7 to 6.2, genes 47 to 79) that keeps nothing and both Desmedt models are empty. The paper's Desmedt pathway result (p 5.12e-36, AUC 0.92 on 198 patients) is close to what a penalty near 1 gives in-sample: 77 pathways, p 2.8e-37, AUC 0.94. The curves follow our model, not the paper's; see fig5.values. On our scores the pathway model beats the gene model on Pawitan only; on Miller it has the higher AUC but the higher p, on Ivshina the gene model wins, and on Desmedt neither model keeps a feature. See fig5.values.

The genomic and combined models are fitted on our pathway scores, which are not the paper's (table2.genomic_univariate). The clinical model matches on Miller (p 3.9e-11 against 2.2e-10, AUC 0.75 against 0.74) and its AUC on Ivshina (0.65), but its Ivshina p is 1.7e-5 against 2.7e-3. On Ivshina, whose arrays are mostly Miller's, the genomic and combined models have smaller p-values than printed and slightly lower AUCs (0.67 against 0.68, 0.69 against 0.71); on Miller both are weaker. The curves follow our model, not the paper's; see fig6.values. Combined beats genomic beats clinical on Ivshina; on Miller our genomic model (AUC 0.73) is below the clinical model (0.75), with 5 pathways instead of the paper's 15. See fig6.values.

Adding clinical features does help it on both sets (AUC 0.81 against 0.73 on Miller, 0.69 against 0.67 on Ivshina). Ivshina is not an independent test set: 232 of its 249 arrays are Miller's.

What came back

The pipeline
pathifier scores, the penalized Cox model with 250 cross-validations, the prognostic index and its cutoffs, the clinical, combined, gene-based and NKI70 models, as the R package pdscox.
The patients
Table 1's counts for all four data sets, once Miller's clinical data were found in breastCancerUPP (GEO has none); left over are a swapped PgR row and rounding in the paper, the size-class boundaries, and one Ivshina tumour under 10 mm (15 against 14).
Fig. 1
11 of its 12 printed p-values (the chi-square and log-rank tests of the clinical factors; not the PAM50 clusters), and the four Kaplan-Meier panels within 2 px (96 to 98% of the published curve pixels).
The clinical model
The same four features (lymph node, size, grade, p53) with coefficients within 0.05 of Table 2, and the four univariate p-values as printed.
Table 3
The genomic model's top 30 genes with their counts and weights, 60 of 60 fields, from the paper's own pathways and hazard ratios.
NKI70
Its log-rank p and AUC on the training set, as printed in Fig. S3.

What stayed buried

  • The paper's pathway scores: on ours, 11 of its 15 selected pathways have univariate p-values more than ten times larger (VIP, LYSOSOME, AKAP13 and LINOLEIC ACID at p 0.5 to 0.8 instead of 2e-6 to 4e-3). On five of them, other seeds, no normalization, no gene filters, no stability option or linear input did not bring them back.
  • So our genomic model keeps 5 pathways (3 of the paper's) instead of 15, and the test sets come out weaker than printed: Desmedt p 0.69 against 3.73e-4.
  • Desmedt's own models: cross-validation keeps no gene and no pathway; the paper's p 5.12e-36 and AUC 0.92 need a penalty far below the cross-validated one.
  • The PAM50 clusters of Fig. 1A and the pathway clusters of Fig. 3: no clustering we tried reaches the printed p-values (best 0.011 against 7.46e-5, and 7.4e-4 against 1.99e-6).
  • Fig. S1: with fewer pathways the AUC hardly falls (median 0.715 to 0.707).

The paper's main claim does not hold on our run: the pathway model is weaker than printed and does not carry to Desmedt. Adding clinical features does help it on both sets (AUC 0.81 against 0.73 on Miller, 0.69 against 0.67 on Ivshina). Ivshina is not an independent test set: 232 of its 249 arrays are Miller's.
